clue.text: Tyson and Ali involved in punches

indicators.note: things involved are tangled up together, so the boxers' names are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the boxer's name taken as written
the other boxer's name taken as written

explanation.surface: Two heavyweight legends trading blows in a famous fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is to attack them physically, which is what a fighter who punches does.

indicators.note: something gone sadly wrong is out of order, so the city's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the French city taken as written

explanation.surface: A lonely traveller feeling melancholy in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can describe something single, with nothing else present: an only child is a child by itself.

indicators.note: about means around, so the writing goes round the examination

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An essay written on the ethical basis of tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's morals are the ethical standards or rules of conduct they live by.

clue.text: Object is to get an annoying person to admit corruption

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the corruption is taken inside the annoying person

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance of a person
rot is decay or moral corruption

explanation.surface: A plan to make some irritating person confess to graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to express disapproval or raise an objection, the verb sense of object.

clue.text: In distribution of income the company is thrifty

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things around, so the letters are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm that shares out its earnings carefully is praised for frugality.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean economical, sparing with money and avoiding waste, as a thrifty person is.

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees
trees that are doomed are destined to come down

explanation.surface: A forester's cry that the best woodland is marked for felling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like an adjective praising the trees, but it stands for the phrase meaning in the first place.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime means first in order or importance, and the phrase marks what comes before everything else.

clue.text: Came in to change the pictures

indicators.note: changing the words alters their arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stepped indoors to swap the paintings on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pictures' is British slang for a film theatre, as in going to the pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is an informal British way of saying going to watch films in a theatre.

clue.text: One shouldn't miss this store opening

definitions.text: One shouldn't miss this store opening

parts.words: One shouldn't miss this store opening
parts.note: surface: a shop launch you ought not to skip
setter's reading: the huge entrance to a farm storehouse, a byword for a target too big to miss

explanation.surface: An advert urging shoppers not to miss a grand shop launch.
explanation.walkthrough: The store is a farm building, not a shop; the idiom says a bad shot could not hit one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is proverbial for a huge, easy target: someone who cannot hit a barn door is a hopeless shot.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: break into a conversation
second meaning: pay one's share towards a collection

explanation.surface: Someone butts into a meeting just to offer their two pennies' worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both cutting into a conversation with a remark and contributing money to a joint fund.

clue.text: See a letter goes to the agent

parts.note: any single letter will do; here it is E
a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Look: a note is being delivered to the secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or notice something, a literary synonym for see.

clue.text: Amazed — and so is the organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging things into order, so the preceding words are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the four words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone surprised, and the whole company equally taken aback.
explanation.walkthrough: The innocent-looking run of little words is the fodder; the last word is the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonished and amazed both mean greatly surprised, as by something unexpected.

parts.note: the indefinite article in its other form
an ode is a lyric poem; the possessive 's supplies the final S

explanation.surface: A critic listing the strong features of a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'an ode's': the possessive ending supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodes are the positive electrodes of a battery or cell, the points where current enters.

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the words are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A perfumed, pretentious child.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant is a person's child, grandchild or later heir, so a form of offspring.

parts.note: surface: everything counted up altogether
setter's reading: the answer is two words that each mean the same thing, so it says the definition two times

explanation.walkthrough: Each of the two words alone means the whole amount, so the phrase states the idea twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum total is the complete amount when everything is added up, which is what all told means.

parts.note: surface: an instruction that something is compulsory
setter's reading: to have something in the sense of owning it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have to' reads as obligation; take 'have' alone as ownership and the clue says that to have is to do this.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, which is the plain sense of the verb have.

clue.text: Framework keels over with added weight

indicators.note: something that keels over is upset and tumbled, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A frame collapses under a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is a supporting structure, whether of bones or of a building, so a framework.

clue.text: Retire from the contest — not up to it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: withdraw a horse or competitor from a race

definitions.note: cryptic: 'it' stands for the answer in the phrase 'up to ___'
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the phrase 'not up to ___' means not good enough

explanation.surface: A competitor pulls out, perhaps because they lack the ability.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half works only if 'it' is the answer itself: something substandard is not up to the required level.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch an entrant is to withdraw it before the race, and the idiom 'up to scratch' means of acceptable quality.

indicators.note: out means disordered or not in place, so the letters are shuffled out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remained at a party, yet was shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stayed' looks like remained, but stays are the stiffening strips of a corset.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is stiffened with stays, so someone wearing one is literally stayed, braced at the waist.

parts.note: surface: workers let off or replaced by their managers
setter's reading: raised knobs on a surface, giving it relief like a raised design

explanation.walkthrough: Bosses are not managers but round raised studs; a surface set with them stands out in relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Something studded is set with knobs or bosses projecting from its surface, so it is decorated in relief.

clue.text: Vulgar chaps start telling a low story

parts.note: base means low and coarse
chaps are men

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter only

explanation.surface: Crude fellows begin recounting a smutty tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The story is a storey, the American spelling of a floor level of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the lowest level of a building, below ground, so a low storey.

indicators.note: something in distress is in a troubled state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A suffering animal moos mournfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' suggests a cow mooing, but the definition is the verb meaning reduces.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate something is to reduce or lessen it, as one lowers a price or a level.

clue.text: It's worn by a woman for a dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short open jacket
second meaning: a lively Spanish dance in triple time

explanation.surface: A garment a woman puts on to go dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a short jacket ending above the waist and a Spanish dance, famously set by Ravel.

clue.text: Nothing in this vessel will be of extravagant style

indicators.note: putting nothing in this vessel gives the style, so the style without nothing gives the vessel

parts.note: the ornate style of 17th-century art and architecture
O is the figure zero

explanation.surface: A ship whose fittings are deliberately plain and unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: add the round zero to the vessel and you get the ornate style, so take it away from the style to find the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing ship with three or more masts, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: A team captain who knows the score?

definitions.text: A team captain who knows the score?

parts.note: a band is a group working together, here of musicians
the captain of a side is its leader

explanation.surface: A sports skipper who keeps track of the points.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the team is a group of musicians and the score is sheet music, not the points tally.
explanation.definitionFit: The person directing a dance or jazz group is its leader, who must know the written music.

parts.note: surface: a sibling of the storyteller
setter's reading: the word for brother as used in the Uncle Remus tales

explanation.walkthrough: In Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus stories the animals are called Brer Rabbit, Brer Fox and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the dialect form of brother used as a title for the animal characters in those tales.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a magistrate or judge
second meaning: a bird's hard mouthpart

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like a court invoice; beak is old British slang for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Beak is slang for a magistrate or schoolmaster, and a bird's beak is its bill.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the original sense of penthouse, a sloping shed against a wall

explanation.surface: Someone expressing a taste for a luxury top-floor flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A penthouse was first a lean-to shed; the luxury rooftop flat is the later sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean to an option is to favour it, and a lean-to is a shed whose roof rests against a wall.

indicators.note: promotion moves someone to a new position, so the letters are moved into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A schooled young officer recruit is in line to move up a rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educated has been taught and instructed, so has been trained in knowledge or skills.
